**Laparotomy** (Danish: *laparotomi*) is defined as open surgery and represents one of the two primary surgical treatment methods systematically documented in the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (AKDB). Its application and proportional use are tracked in comparison to [[laparoskopi]] (minimally invasive surgery) [^src1]. The systematic quantification and regional comparison of these two central surgical techniques serve as a foundation for quality development and political decision-making within acute surgery across [[danmark|Danmark]] [^src1].

Over a three-year period, national data from the AKDB reveals a steady decline in the proportion of acute surgical procedures performed as open laparotomies, reflecting a shift toward laparoscopy. In the reporting period from September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023, there were 3,214 acute surgical procedures, of which 1,692 (52.64%) were laparotomies [^src1]. This proportion decreased to 48.66% (1,580 out of 3,247 procedures) in the 2023–2024 period [^src1], and dropped further to 44.18% (1,436 out of 3,250 procedures) between September 1, 2024, and August 31, 2025 [^src1].

In addition to tracking the surgical approach, the database monitors anesthesia practices associated with open surgery as part of national quality indicators. A specific development target for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] requires that more than 60% of patients undergoing laparotomy receive [[epidural]] anesthesia [^src2]. In the most recent reporting period (September 1, 2024 – August 31, 2025), the national proportion of patients receiving epidurals during laparotomies reached 66.7% (95% CI: 64.2–69.1), indicating that the quality target is being met at the national level, though significant inter-hospital variation remains [^src2].
